summary: Create a new project from a template
description: Creates the folder (if needed) and writes the project file <name>.vcprj and the sources of the template, per target system under src/<system>/. The folder must not contain a .vcprj yet.
With --structure, the folders and layout of a project structure are added. vcc new --list shows templates, variants and project structures with the possible target systems.

args.name: folder
args.help: Project folder. Its name is the project name if --name is missing. Not needed with --list.

options.help: Target systems, separated by commas. Each gets its own sources under src/<system>/. The template must support the system.
File template: assembler program, BASIC or only the project file with src/.
Variant of the template. cartridge creates an 8 KB cartridge instead of a program (asm-hello only; c64, atari8, vic20).

Project structure: creates folders and enters the layout in the project file. Your own templates from structures.json are also possible. The earlier German names (einfach, gross, mehrsystem, bibliothek, spiel) are still accepted.
Character set of the project: auto = your ROM as a reference, otherwise the own default set as a copy; own = always the own default set (can be passed on, with HERKUNFT.txt); none = none.
Project name (letters, digits, _ and -, at most 48 characters). Sets the name of the .vcprj.
List project structures, templates and variants with their target systems. Creates nothing.

options.default_text: VC_DATA, otherwise next to the program or in the working folder

examples.title: BASIC project with a project structure
examples.cmd: vcc new demo --target c64,vic20 --template basic-hello --structure multisystem

notes: The template empty exists for c64, c128, plus4, vic20, atari8 and mega65. asm-hello also exists for pet, and basic-hello for pet.
Without your own ROM, auto puts the own set VC-Standard (CC0) in graphics/vc-standard/. Systems without an own set (PET) get nothing.
The folders and files that were created are printed.
